name: jscpd
description: Copy/paste detection in the editor: exact, renamed, near-miss, similar and semantic clones, dead code and complexity from jscpd --lsp, and a migration view for jscpd --compare.

jscpd.path.description: Path to the jscpd executable. Empty: the extension looks in PATH, then uses or downloads a release build.

jscpd.download.description: What to do when jscpd is neither at `jscpd.path` nor in PATH: ask before downloading a release build, download without asking, or never download.

jscpd.version.description: The release to download: `latest` or a tag such as `v5.4.0`.

jscpd.analyses.clones.description: Report exact, renamed and near-miss copies. On by default in the server; off switches them off for every project.

jscpd.analyses.similarFunctions.description: Report JavaScript and TypeScript functions whose syntax trees have the same shape (`--similarity`). Off: whatever the project's .jscpd.json says.

jscpd.analyses.semantic.description: Report functions that do the same job with different code (`--semantic`). Needs the embedding model, which jscpd offers to download. Off: whatever the project's .jscpd.json says.

jscpd.analyses.deadCode.description: Report unused files, exports, symbols, imports and members (`--dead-code`). Off: whatever the project's .jscpd.json says.

jscpd.analyses.complexity.description: Report functions and files above the complexity limit. Off: whatever the project's .jscpd.json says.

jscpd.allFiles.description: Also publish the diagnostics of closed files, so the Problems panel lists the whole project.

jscpd.clones.warningTokens.description: Clones of at least this many tokens are warnings, smaller ones information. Empty: as the project's .jscpd.json says, else every clone is a warning.

jscpd.similarFunctions.similarity.description: How much of their syntax-tree shape two functions must share to count as similar. At 0.85 the project's own value applies.

jscpd.complexity.functionLimit.description: A function above this cyclomatic complexity gets a diagnostic. At 15 the project's own value applies.

jscpd.settings.markdownDescription: Keys of `.jscpd.json` applied to every project on top of its own config, for example `{ "minTokens": 70, "ignoreIdentifiers": true }`.

jscpd.args.markdownDescription: Extra arguments for `jscpd --lsp`, for example `["--semantic-url", "http://localhost:11434/v1"]`. Not `--config` or paths: the server reads each project's own `.jscpd.json`.

jscpd.decorations.description: Show an icon in the gutter and a mark in the overview ruler for each finding, colored by kind.

jscpd.compare.ignore.description: Folders `jscpd --compare` leaves out of both sides, comma-separated globs.

jscpd.compare.watch.description: Run the last comparison again when a file in either folder is saved.

jscpd.trace.server.description: Log the messages between the extension and jscpd.

commands.title: Download or update the jscpd binary

view/title.when: view == jscpd.clones || view == jscpd.deadCode || view == jscpd.complexity

viewsWelcome.contents:
jscpd is not running.
[Download jscpd](command:jscpd.downloadBinary)
Or set the path to an installed binary in the settings.
No clones in the open projects.

Measure a port: pick the folder you port from and the folder you port to, and jscpd pairs their functions.
[Compare two folders](command:jscpd.compare)
No dead code reported. Turn the analysis on with `jscpd.analyses.deadCode` or in the project's `.jscpd.json`.
Nothing over the complexity limit. Turn the analysis on with `jscpd.analyses.complexity` or in the project's `.jscpd.json`.

colors.description: Functions and files over the complexity limit

scripts.test: npm run build && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json && node ./out/test/runTest.js
scripts.package: npm run check && npm run build && vsce package --no-dependencies --baseContentUrl https://github.com/kucherenko/jscpd-ide/blob/HEAD/vscode --baseImagesUrl https://github.com/kucherenko/jscpd-ide/raw/HEAD/vscode
